events.title: US CPI for September released
events.why_it_matters: Headline inflation sits at 3.4% y/y with a 7.3% gas-price spike and core at 2.4%; this print directly reprices odds of a second Fed hike at the Oct 27-28 FOMC.
events.what_to_watch: Core m/m vs ~0.3% consensus and gas passthrough; a hot print pushes hike odds up and long yields higher.

events.title: Fed Beige Book released
events.why_it_matters: Regional anecdotes at 2pm ET color the FOMC backdrop two weeks before the decision.
events.what_to_watch: Tone on labor softness vs price pressure in tariff-exposed sectors.

events.title: FOMC meeting Oct 27-28: second hike on the table
events.why_it_matters: With August PCE signaling 'further hikes likely' and a hawkish backdrop, prediction markets show live odds of a second hike — this meeting is the biggest scheduled macro risk of the window.
events.what_to_watch: CPI (Oct 14) and jobs data into the meeting; dot-plot/presser language on further tightening.

events.title: September retail sales report
events.why_it_matters: Consumer resilience data lands mid-window and feeds the Fed hike debate.
events.what_to_watch: Control-group ex-autos sales vs modest consensus; weakness would cut hike odds.

events.title: Shutdown averted; CR funds government through Dec 11
events.why_it_matters: The Oct 1 shutdown risk was resolved when Trump signed a stopgap, removing a near-term headwind but queuing a December fight.
events.what_to_watch: Appropriations negotiations ahead of Dec 11; data delays if a lapse recurs.

events.title: US-China Board of Trade product lists for tariff cuts
events.why_it_matters: Following the Sept 24-25 Trump-Xi meeting, the White House listed goods for potential tariff cuts under the new bilateral 'Board of Trade' mechanism — a de-escalation lever for trade-sensitive sectors.
events.what_to_watch: Whether lists become binding proclamations and Chinese reciprocal lists.

events.title: Emergency Tax Relief on Diesel Fuel executive order
events.why_it_matters: Diesel tax relief partially offsets the fuel-cost squeeze from the Iran/Ukraine supply shocks (EO 14435).
events.what_to_watch: Revenue offsets and whether the relief is extended or converted to law.

events.title: Houthi missile/drone attacks on Saudi airports (Oct 6-12) and Saudi response risk
events.why_it_matters: Deadliest Gulf attack series in a decade (20+ killed) puts Saudi oil infrastructure and the Strait of Hormuz risk premium back in play; OPEC+ cited war-limited supply in holding output steady.
events.what_to_watch: Saudi retaliation, Iran proxy escalation, and attacks on Red Sea shipping routes.

events.title: OPEC+ holds November output targets steady
events.why_it_matters: Output kept unchanged as war limits supply — no bearish quota surprise, but supply-risk premium remains in crude.
events.what_to_watch: Monthly IEA/OPEC reports this week for demand-revision direction.

events.title: Russia diesel export shock / Ukraine war supply risk
events.why_it_matters: Disrupted Russian diesel supply plus the Saudi-Houthi war is driving fuel inflation, a key input to the hawkish CPI/Fed story.
events.what_to_watch: Refined-product inventories and whether US-Iran 'energy ceasefire' diplomacy holds.

events.title: IMF-World Bank annual meetings; IMF warns of global resilience limits
events.why_it_matters: IMF explicitly warns the global economy 'could soon test the limits of resilience' amid tariff-driven trade deficit blowout ($105.6B) and war shocks.
events.what_to_watch: World Economic Outlook growth revisions and downgrade language for the US and China.

events.title: ECB rate decision Oct 29 — hold at 2.50% expected
events.why_it_matters: Markets price ~87% odds of no change at 2.50%; the press conference matters more than the decision for euro-area and rate-sensitive equities.
events.what_to_watch: Lagarde's language on energy-driven inflation vs weak growth.

events.title: ASML Q3 results — record sales, AI demand surge
events.why_it_matters: ASML beat with record €11.7B net sales (+55% y/y) and raised guidance — the semicap bellwether for the AI capex cycle.
events.what_to_watch: Book-to-bill and 2027 EUV demand commentary; effect on US semis today.

events.title: TSMC Q3 earnings and Q4 guidance
events.why_it_matters: Record $46.7B September-quarter revenue is confirmed; margins and capex guidance are the single biggest read on AI chip demand for the whole sector.
events.what_to_watch: Gross margin vs record mix, 2026 capex, and any tariff/export-control caution on China sales.

events.title: Big bank earnings: JPM, BAC, MS, BLK, GS
events.why_it_matters: Kicks off Q3 earnings season and reveals trading, credit, and NIM dynamics under a higher-rate backdrop.
events.what_to_watch: Credit-loss provisions and deal/trading pipeline commentary.

events.title: Tesla earnings (Mon Oct 19) and Netflix (Tue Oct 20)
events.why_it_matters: Two of the most actively traded names headline next week; Tesla's margins/delivery guidance and Netflix's ads tier drive sector rotation.
events.what_to_watch: Tesla auto gross margin ex-credits and Netflix subscriber/ad revenue commentary.

events.title: Staples & industrials mega-cap earnings wave (PG, JNJ, KO, IBM, GE-type names)
events.why_it_matters: 57 companies report next week; a dense blue-chip wave will test whether 3.4% headline inflation is compressing consumer and input margins.
events.what_to_watch: Tariff-cost and diesel/fuel cost pass-through commentary.

events.title: Apple-Epic Supreme Court appeal (27% App Store fee) in new term
events.why_it_matters: SCOTUS hearing the Apple-Epic fee appeal threatens App Store economics with platform-wide implications for digital-goods margins.
events.what_to_watch: Argument date confirmation on the SCOTUS calendar; DOJ split adds uncertainty.

events.title: Trump-Xi September summit and tariff de-escalation track
events.why_it_matters: The Washington Trump-Xi meeting produced the Board of Trade mechanism — the most significant US-China thaw since tariffs began; still fragile.
events.what_to_watch: Implementation of tariff-cut lists and any snapback rhetoric.

events.title: US trade deficit hits $105.6B — widest since before tariffs
events.why_it_matters: A record deficit undercuts the tariff strategy narrative and could trigger fresh White House trade actions.
events.what_to_watch: Subsequent tariffs or Board of Trade acceleration; Q3 GDP net-exports drag.

events.title: China Q3 GDP and September activity data
events.why_it_matters: China's Q3 growth print tests whether the Trump-Xi détente is translating into domestic demand or masking continued weakness.
events.what_to_watch: Property-sector investment and retail sales; any fresh stimulus announcement.

events.title: November 2026 midterm elections approach (4 weeks out)
events.why_it_matters: The CR was passed in the 'final stretch of the campaign'; a possible divided or flipped Congress after Nov 3 reprices tax, tariff, and regulation expectations.
events.what_to_watch: Polling trends and policy-heavy campaign rhetoric on energy, crypto, and antitrust.

events.title: Yemen government offensive against Houthis
events.why_it_matters: Escalating Saudi/Yemeni ground campaign against the Houthis raises the odds of wider Gulf conflict hitting oil flows.
events.what_to_watch: Red Sea shipping disruption and Saudi strikes on Iranian-linked targets.

top_risks: Hot September CPI today (gas +7.3% passthrough) raising Fed second-hike odds into the Oct 27-28 FOMC — rate-sensitive sectors (Real Estate, Utilities, long-duration tech) vulnerable
Saudi-Houthi escalation: attacks on Riyadh airports plus a Saudi ground offensive create an oil-supply tail risk to Hormuz/Red Sea flows
Fed 'second hike' scenario with accompanying hawkish dots would pressure equities broadly
Russian diesel shock sustaining fuel inflation and squeezing industrials/transport margins
December 11 government funding deadline teeing up a pre-midterm fiscal fight
top_opportunities: AI semicap momentum: ASML record quarter (Oct 14) sets up TSMC's Oct 15 report — strong TSMC guidance would lift the whole AI complex
US-China Board of Trade tariff-cut lists: upside for industrials, retailers, and China-exposed tech if implemented
Bank earnings this week with higher-rate tailwind on net interest income
Diesel fuel tax relief EO (Oct 5) easing transport/industrial cost pressure
Netflix (Oct 20) ad-tier and subscriber growth as a Communication Services catalyst
summary: The window is dominated by inflation-vs-hike risk: today's September CPI (3.4% headline backdrop, core 2.4%) directly sets up an Oct 27-28 FOMC where a second hike is genuinely live. Geopolitical fuel-supply shocks (Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia, Russian diesel disruption) are feeding the inflation problem while the US-China Board of Trade détente provides an offsetting de-escalation channel. Heavy AI-semiconductor earnings (ASML today, TSMC Oct 15) plus a dense blue-chip wave next week give constant catalysts through the window.
